items: Title: Social / Information Mechanics
Player Safe: Players can interact, comfort, persuade, or earn trust Nettle when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.

No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A frightened scout with forest mud on both knees and one eye always on the exits. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

Rolls: entity-nettle-engage-nettle entity-nettle Engage Nettle Engage Nettle Presence Knowledge Instinct Presence Knowledge, Instinct 12 Choose the trait from the player's method, not the entity type. A flat read of Nettle hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Block1: Nettle NET-ul a frightened forest scout trying not to be seen A frightened Bramble scout who shows the camp is people, not bandits. A non-violent encounter that tests mercy; how the party treats Nettle echoes through the whole Union. They are scouting, not attacking, and one act of cruelty here teaches them that mercy is foolish. A way forward A grounded question A scene-specific clue seed Cornered and trembling, desperate not to prove their own fears right. Mercy that visibly costs the party something, so it reads as real and not convenient.

Block2: Get back to camp without proving mercy is foolish. Keep their people alive without learning to hate everyone outside the trees. Get back to camp without proving mercy is foolish. Keep their people alive without learning to hate everyone outside the trees. Soft-hearted and quick-footed, frozen between flight and trust. Rubs a seed-charm from home whenever a choice sounds like betrayal either way. Wants to keep their people alive without learning to hate everyone outside the trees. I am not the one who wanted blades first. Nettle can name who did not want the ambush to go violent. Being handed to officials, disappointing Kett, and watching the camp starve anyway. Gentle voices, clear promises, and food that is offered without a bargain first. Sudden movement, corporate badges, and adults calling fear weakness. Gentle voices, clear promises, and food that is offered without a bargain...
